@appxtbl-rq1-differences answers, for each pair of motives with opposite predicted signs, whether the coefficient of the motive predicted positive exceeded that of the motive predicted negative.

::: {#appxtbl-rq1-differences}

```{r}
#| label: appx-rq1-differences
d <- rq1_differences_value
rh_table(
  tibble::tibble(
    outcome = rh_blank_repeated(rh_label(d$outcome_key, labels)),
    pair = paste0(rh_label(d$motive_positive, labels), " minus ", rh_label_inline(d$motive_negative, labels)),
    difference = rh_fmt_est_ci(d$median, d$lower, d$upper, 2, bold = d$credible & d$interpretable)
  ),
  col_labels = c(outcome = "Facet", pair = "Motive predicted positive minus motive predicted negative",
                 difference = paste0("Difference [", ci_pct, " CrI]")),
  source_note = paste0("Posterior median of the difference between the two standardised coefficients in the same regression, ",
                       "formed in every posterior draw, with its central ", ci_pct, " credible interval. ",
                       "Bold estimate: its interval excludes zero.")
)
```

Differences between the coefficients of two motives with opposite predicted signs.
:::

@appxtbl-rq1-partials answers how strongly two motives overlap once the other three motives, age, gender and income are held constant.

::: {#appxtbl-rq1-partials}

```{r}

rh_table(
  tibble::tibble(
    pair = paste0(rh_label(pc$motive_a, labels), " and ", rh_label_inline(pc$motive_b, labels)),
    partial = rh_fmt_est_ci(pc$median, pc$lower, pc$upper, 2, bounded = TRUE, bold = pc$credible & pc$interpretable)
  ),
  col_labels = c(pair = "Motives", partial = paste0("Partial correlation [", ci_pct, " CrI]")),
  source_note = paste0("Posterior median of the partial correlation, conditional on the other three motives, age, gender ",
                       "and income, from the joint model of the five motive scores, with its central ", ci_pct, " credible interval. ",
                       "Bold estimate: its interval excludes zero.")
)
```

Partial correlations of the five motives.
:::

## S2 Measurement {#sec-measurement-detail .unnumbered}

__Question.__ How were the response options used, how were the reliability
intervals obtained, and how well do the confirmatory models fit the item
responses?

The loadings and the latent correlations of the
confirmatory models are in `r sec_link("sec-appendix-measurement")`; the
unstandardised loadings with their standard errors are in the data file

### S2.1 Item Distributions {.unnumbered}

@suppltbl-item-distributions-motives and @suppltbl-item-distributions-orientation
answer how the six response options were used for each item, the information
on which the choice of the estimator for ordered categories rests. The response
counts retain the original item
coding after participant exclusions. Percentages use the nonmissing responses
to each item as denominator. Response options selected by nobody are retained
with a count of zero; an item
with unanswered cells is marked, and its number of missing answers is in the
table note.

The sufficient summary statistics of the measurement models are provided as
machine-readable files: the item-by-item polychoric
correlation matrix in `r s1_value$summary_files[1]` and the item
thresholds in `r s1_value$summary_files[2]`, beside the file of all
pairwise standardised residuals, `r s1_value$residuals_file`. A
secondary analysis can refit any of the confirmatory models from those two
files alone.

::: {#suppltbl-item-distributions-motives}

```{r}
#| label: suppl-item-distributions-motives
```

## S3 Bayesian Multiple Regressions (RQ1) {#sec-supplement-regressions .unnumbered}

__Research question.__ `r rh_prereg_question(prereg, "RQ1")`

### S3.1 Prior-Predictive Checks {#sec-supplement-prior-predictive .unnumbered}

Draws from the priors alone, back-transformed to the response scale with the
fixed standardisation constants of each model's own sample, place a small share
of the simulated responses outside the range the items admit; the share per
facet, prior width and likelihood family is in @suppltbl-prior-predictive. The
check runs on the actual design for every
width of the sweep and for both likelihood families; simulated outcomes are
never standardised again. @suppltbl-prior-predictive answers whether the priors,
before the data are seen, imply answers within and around the response scale.
`r rh_prior_pred_constant_text(s4_value$prior_predictive)`

::: {#suppltbl-prior-predictive}

```{r}
#| label: suppl-prior-predictive
rh_prior_pred_table(s4_value$prior_predictive, labels, analysis_plan = analysis_plan,
                    target = "supplement_model_checks")
```

Prior predictive checks: percentiles of the answers simulated from the priors alone and the shares outside the response range, per facet and model.
:::

### S3.2 Prior and Likelihood Sensitivity {#sec-prior-sensitivity .unnumbered}


#### Prior-Width Comparison {.unnumbered}

The preregistration specifies the priors and the
robustness procedures (AP6).

@suppltbl-prior-sweep answers whether a coefficient's classification depends on
the prior: every motive coefficient under each of the three priors.

::: {#suppltbl-prior-sweep}

```{r}
#| label: suppl-prior-sweep
rh_sensitivity_table(s3_value$sensitivity, labels, analysis_plan = analysis_plan,
                     target = "supplement_prior_sensitivity")
```

Every motive coefficient under each of the three priors.
:::

Across the `r rh_fmt_count(n_sweep_widths)` widths of the sweep,
`r sweep_credibility_text` (@suppltbl-prior-sweep).
`r if (sweep_interpretable) paste0("For these fits, ", sweep_sign_text, ".") else "The table is retained for diagnosis; its stability classifications are not interpreted."`

#### Local Power Scaling {.unnumbered}

Power scaling ran for each of the
`r rh_fmt_count(n_ps_blocks)` blocks of priors (`r ps_block_text`) on its own
and once for all priors together. Importance sampling is labelled reliable when
the largest Pareto k across the four perturbations is below
$\min(0.7, 1 - 1/\log_{10}(S))$, where $S$ is the number of saved posterior draws;
otherwise it is labelled unreliable. Missing diagnostics or draw counts are
labelled unavailable. Sensitivity flags from unreliable or unavailable calculations
are retained for transparency but are not interpreted.
`r suppl_power_scaling_text` Neither
check changes a classification of the Results section, and neither is used to
select a preferred result after seeing the data; local insensitivity is not
global robustness.

```{r}
#| label: suppl-priorsense
#| output: asis
rh_float_show(
  rh_priorsense_table(s3_value$priorsense_flagged, labels,
                      basename(analysis_plan$data_files$result_files$prior_power_scaling)),
  id = "priorsense", prefix = "suppltbl",
  caption = "The power-scaling entries flagged with a diagnosis, per block of priors."
)
```

@supplfig-prior-posterior
answers how far the data
moved each motive coefficient away from its prior: the preregistered prior,
`r rh_normal_prior(analysis_plan$priors$slope_sd_primary)`, beside the posterior, drawn as the
normal density with the coefficient's posterior median and posterior standard
deviation. The posterior under a flat prior, which would show the data alone, is
not drawn: no flat-prior fit exists.

::: {#supplfig-prior-posterior}

```{r}
#| label: suppl-prior-posterior
#| fig-height: 8
rh_prior_posterior_plot(s3_value$coefficients_primary, analysis_plan, labels,
                        density_data = s3_value$prior_posterior_density)
```

Prior and posterior of each motive coefficient in the four regressions with the preregistered prior.
:::

#### Posterior-Predictive Checks {#sec-model-checks .unnumbered}

@suppltbl-posterior-predictive sets the observed
`r join_and(unname(pp_stat_words[setdiff(checks$stats, c("mean", "sd"))]))` of each
facet against the band of the replicated data and gives the one-sided
posterior predictive *p*-value of every statistic; the note of that table
states the direction of that value, which for the minimum runs opposite to a
heavy-tail reading. @supplfig-posterior-predictive shows the same fits as
densities against the observed distribution. The displayed table focuses on
skewness, excess kurtosis, minimum, and maximum. Predictive checks of the mean
and standard deviation are retained in the accompanying data file
(`r basename(analysis_plan$data_files$result_files$posterior_predictive_checks)`).
It answers whether data simulated from each fitted model look like the observed
facet scores.

::: {#suppltbl-posterior-predictive}

```{r}
#| label: suppl-posterior-predictive
rh_pp_stats_table(s4_value$posterior_predictive, labels, analysis_plan = analysis_plan,
                  target = "supplement_model_checks")
```

Posterior predictive checks: each observed statistic against the range of the data sets simulated from the fitted model, with the one-sided posterior predictive p-value.
:::

::: {#supplfig-posterior-predictive}

```{r}
#| label: suppl-pp-plot
rh_pp_plot(NULL, labels = labels, density_data = s4_value$predictive_density)
```

Posterior predictive distributions against the observed distribution of each facet.
:::

#### Refit With Heavier Tails {#sec-supplement-student .unnumbered}

The Gaussian likelihood is the preregistered choice, and a Student-t refit is
a descriptive complement that runs only for a facet whose tail statistic is
more extreme than its replicated band on one side.
`r tail_text` A refit
never changes a verdict of the Results section.

`r pp_outside_text` The preregistered refit addresses heavy tails only: it
replaces the Gaussian likelihood by a Student-t one with a fixed
degrees-of-freedom parameter, which widens the tails and does nothing about asymmetry or a
bounded response range. A misfit in the skewness of a bounded, standardised
Likert score is therefore reported here and not treated, because treating it
would mean changing a preregistered likelihood after seeing the data.

`r robustness_lead`

```{r}
#| label: suppl-student-robustness
#| output: asis
rh_float_show(
  rh_robustness_table(s4_value$likelihood_comparison, labels, analysis_plan = analysis_plan,
                      target = "supplement_model_checks"),
  id = "student-robustness", prefix = "suppltbl",
  caption = "The coefficients of the Gaussian model beside those of the refit allowing heavier tails."
)
```

`r student_r2_text`

```{r}
#| label: suppl-student-r2
#| output: asis
rh_float_show(
  build_saved_student_r2_table(regression_r2_summaries_value, analysis_plan, labels),
  id = "student-r2", prefix = "suppltbl",
  caption = "Explained variance of the refits allowing heavier tails beside that of the Gaussian model."
)
```

### S3.3 Validity Gate {#sec-additional-diagnostics .unnumbered}

`r diagnostics_lead_text` The
preregistration states the diagnostic rules (AP6).
`r diagnostics_constant_text`

::: {#suppltbl-diagnostics}

```{r}
#| label: suppl-diagnostics
rh_diagnostics_table(diagnostics_value$diagnostics, analysis_plan, labels,
                     additional = diagnostics_additional_value, target = "supplement_sampling_diagnostics")
```

Sampling diagnostics of every regression fit.
:::

## S4 Bayesian Network Analysis (RQ3) {#sec-network-detail .unnumbered}

__Research question.__ `r rh_prereg_question(prereg, "RQ3")`

### S4.1 Full-Data and Bagged Network {#sec-supplement-network-stability .unnumbered}

The edge decisions of the Results section come from the bagged posterior. This
section sets the bagged network against
the full-data network, the network fitted once to the whole
sample, under the same settings, and reports how stable the decisions are
across the resamples. The bagged network is the preregistered estimate; the
comparison is descriptive and shows how much the resampling moves the
decisions. `r network_agreement_text`

@suppltbl-network-changed-edges lists the
edges they disagree on; `r opposite_text`. @appxfig-network-stability shows, for every
edge, how its inclusion probability varies across the bootstrap resamples;
@supplfig-network-pip plots the two inclusion probabilities against each
other, and @appxfig-network-side-by-side draws the two graphs side by side.
@supplfig-network-pip answers how far bagging moves the inclusion probability of
each edge: the dashed lines mark the inclusion probabilities at which an edge
is present (`r rh_fmt(s5_value$comparison$thresholds$pip_include[1], 3, bounded = TRUE)`, a Bayes
factor of `r rh_fmt_bf(analysis_plan$network$bf_include)`) and absent
(`r rh_fmt(s5_value$comparison$thresholds$pip_exclude[1], 3, bounded = TRUE)`, a Bayes factor of
`r rh_fmt_bf(analysis_plan$network$bf_exclude)`).

::: {#supplfig-network-pip}

```{r}
#| label: suppl-network-pip
rh_network_pip_scatter(s5_value$comparison, labels)
```

Inclusion probability of every edge in the full-data network against its inclusion probability in the bagged network.
:::

@suppltbl-network-changed-edges answers which edges change their decision
between the full-data network and the bagged network, and how often a single
resample reaches either threshold for them.

::: {#suppltbl-network-changed-edges}

```{r}
#| label: suppl-network-changed-edges
rh_network_changed_edges_table(s5_value$comparison, labels)
```

The edges whose decision differs between the full-data network and the bagged network.
:::

### S4.2 Edge-Prior Sensitivity {#sec-supplement-edge-prior .unnumbered}

The classifications also depend on the prior probability that an edge belongs
in the graph, because the rule compares posterior odds with prior odds. The
network was therefore
refitted on all rows of the network sample at each of `r edge_prior_text`,
with the decision thresholds unchanged. Most edges keep their classification
across the unbagged full-data refits, and
`r edge_prior_moving_text`. Stability of the bagged classifications across
edge priors is not evaluated by this comparison. This comparison is descriptive:
the reported classifications are the bagged ones at `r edge_prior_prereg`.
Every edge's result under each prior is reported in @suppltbl-network-prior-sweep.
The table answers whether the decision of the full-data network depends on the
assumed prior probability that an edge exists.

::: {#suppltbl-network-prior-sweep}

```{r}
#| label: suppl-network-prior-sweep
build_saved_network_prior_sweep_table(s5_value$prior_sweep, labels)
```

Decision of the full-data network for every edge under each prior inclusion probability.
:::

## S5 Exploratory Factor Analyses (SRQ1) {#sec-supplement-efa .unnumbered}

__Research question.__ `r rh_prereg_question(prereg, "SRQ1")`

Reliability and dimensionality answer different questions: omega and alpha
describe how consistently a scale's items vary together, whereas the
exploratory analyses ask how many dimensions the items suggest. Each of the
`r rh_fmt_count(n_scale_efas)` scales is analysed on its own, and the
`r rh_fmt_count(n_sets)` item sets of the analysis plan are analysed together:
each names the scales analysed together, and the number of factors expected is
the number of scales it holds. The number of factors each of the
`r rh_fmt_count(n_count_indices)` criteria suggests,
the correspondence between the estimated factors and the
intended scales, the loading clarity and the item membership are in
`r sec_link("sec-appendix-efa")`.

The solutions use polychoric correlations, WLS extraction and the primary
`r analysis_plan$factor_analysis$rotation_primary` rotation. Every item is
assigned to the factor with its largest absolute loading. The complete
loading matrices of every solution are in the data file
`r basename(analysis_plan$data_files$result_files$efa_loadings)`, and the complete
item membership of every solution in
`r basename(analysis_plan$data_files$result_files$efa_membership)`.

For every examined solution, the
single-scale solutions included, @suppltbl-efa-variance gives the share of the
item variance each factor accounts for and the running total. It answers how much of the item variance each solution
and each of its factors accounts for.

::: {#suppltbl-efa-variance}

```{r}
#| label: suppl-efa-variance
rh_efa_set_variance_table(s1_value$efa_variance, s1_value$correspondence$membership, factor_sets,
                          s1_value$factor_number_criteria, labels, target = "supplement_measurement")
```

Variance explained by every examined solution, in the primary rotation.
:::
